## 1. PCI PM callbacks in `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c`

`const struct dev_pm_ops i915_pm_ops` (attached to the PCI driver via `i915_pci_driver.driver.pm`):

| PM hook | callback |
|---|---|
| `.prepare` | `i915_pm_prepare` |
| `.suspend` | **`i915_pm_suspend`** |
| `.suspend_late` | `i915_pm_suspend_late` |
| `.suspend_noirq` | `i915_pm_suspend_noirq` |
| `.resume_early` / `.resume` | `i915_pm_resume_early` / `i915_pm_resume` |
| `.complete` | `i915_pm_complete` |
| `.freeze` / `.freeze_late` | `i915_pm_freeze` / `i915_pm_freeze_late` |
| `.thaw_early` / `.thaw` | `i915_pm_thaw_early` → `i915_pm_resume_early`, `i915_pm_thaw` → `i915_pm_resume` |
| `.poweroff` | **`i915_pm_suspend`** (same function reused) |
| `.poweroff_late` / `.poweroff_noirq` | `i915_pm_poweroff_late` / `i915_pm_poweroff_noirq` |
| `.restore_early` / `.restore` | `i915_pm_restore_early` → `i915_pm_resume_early`, `i915_pm_restore` → `i915_pm_resume` |
| `.runtime_suspend` | `intel_runtime_suspend` |
| `.runtime_resume` | `intel_runtime_resume` |

## 2. Call chains reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

Only two PM entry points reach it, and both are the *same* function pointer:

```
pm_generic / PCI core
  ├─ dev_pm_ops.suspend   ─► i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
  └─ dev_pm_ops.poweroff  ─► i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
                                 │
                                 ├─ i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
                                 └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
```

Sibling (not via `i915_pm_suspend`) paths that also reach `i915_drm_suspend`:
```
i915_pm_freeze          ─► i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)   [+ i915_drm_suspend_late(..., false)]
i915_driver_shutdown    ─► i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)   [+ i915_drm_suspend_late(..., true)]
```
Late/noirq stages fan out separately:
```
i915_pm_suspend_late    ─► i915_drm_suspend_late(drm, false)
i915_pm_suspend_noirq   ─► i915_drm_suspend_noirq(drm, false)
i915_pm_poweroff_late   ─► i915_drm_suspend_late(drm, true)
i915_pm_poweroff_noirq  ─► i915_drm_suspend_noirq(drm, true)
i915_pm_freeze_late     ─► i915_drm_suspend_late(drm, false)
```

**Note:** there is no symbol `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` in this tree. The runtime-PM hook is named **`intel_runtime_suspend`** (`.runtime_suspend = intel_runtime_suspend`).

## 3. Which callers of `i915_pm_suspend` also call the runtime-suspend hook?

**None.** The system-suspend chain (`.suspend`/`.poweroff` → `i915_pm_suspend` → `i915_drm_suspend`) and the runtime chain (`.runtime_suspend` → `intel_runtime_suspend`) are entirely disjoint at the i915 level — they only share leaf helpers:

| leaf helper | `i915_drm_suspend*` | `intel_runtime_suspend` |
|---|---|---|
| `intel_irq_uninstall` | ✔ | ✔ |
| `i915_gem_suspend` | ✔ | — |
| `i915_gem_runtime_suspend` | — | ✔ |
| `intel_gt_runtime_suspend` | — | ✔ |
| `intel_pxp_runtime_suspend(dev_priv->pxp)` | — | ✔ |
| `intel_display_driver_suspend_access` | ✔ | ✔ |
| `intel_dp_mst_suspend` / `intel_hpd_cancel_work` | ✔ | — |

## 4. `dev_priv` data flow: `i915_drm_suspend` → display suspend

The target symbol today is `intel_display_driver_suspend()` (formerly `intel_display_suspend`), declared in `display/intel_display_driver.h`:

```
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
  │  struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);      // device → i915
  ▼
i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)                      // passed &i915->drm
  │  struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);        // drm_device → dev_priv
  │  struct intel_display *display     = dev_priv->display;   // dev_priv → display
  │  pci_power_t opregion_target_state;
  │
  │  disable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(&dev_priv->runtime_pm);      // dev_priv used for RPM
  │  i915_gem_suspend(i915);                                  // dev_priv used for GEM
  │  opregion_target_state = suspend_to_idle(dev_priv) ? PCI_D1 : PCI_D3cold;
  │
  ├─► intel_display_driver_suspend(display)   ◄── dev_priv->display is the only thing handed down
  ├─► intel_dp_mst_suspend(display)
  ├─► intel_hpd_cancel_work(display)
  ├─► intel_display_driver_suspend_access(display)
  ├─► intel_opregion_suspend(display, opregion_target_state)
  └─  enable_rpm_wakeref_asserts(&dev_priv->runtime_pm);
```

Key point of the data flow: `dev_priv` is **not** propagated into the display layer. It is narrowed once — `display = dev_priv->display` — and from `intel_display_driver_suspend()` onward everything operates on the opaque `struct intel_display *` (using `display->drm`, `display->wq.*`, etc.), which is the display/core decoupling boundary. `dev_priv` itself stays in `i915_drm_suspend` for GEM (`i915_gem_suspend`), runtime-PM asserts (`&dev_priv->runtime_pm`), and the `suspend_to_idle(dev_priv)` decision that produces `opregion_target_state`.
